DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 85 s. 2021 09 July 2021 CarloDrizPhoto carlodrizphoto@qmail.com Sir: This has reference to your earlier e-mail asking whether a Punong Barangay, whose wife owns a processed food factory, gives out relief goods with brands similar to those coming from the factory violates the rule on conflict of interest. At the outset, it is noted that the query is not clear whether the relief goods being given away by the Punong Barangay were procured with public or private funds. Be that as it may, if the aforesaid relief goods were procured with the Punong Barangay"s own money, then we find no legal infirmity even if he buys the goods from his wife's own processed food factory. However, if the said goods were bought using public funds, then we agree with you that there is conflict of interest on the part of the Punong Barangay. Under RA 6713, otherwise known as the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees, Section 3 (i) thereof provides that conflict of interest arises when a public official or employee is a member of a board, an officer, or a substantial stockholder of a private corporation or owner or has a substantial interest in a business, and the interest of such corporation or business, or his rights or duties therein, may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty. Since it was stated that the processed food factory is owned by his wife, then the Punong Barangay appears to have substantial interest in said business. Also, the interest of such business may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty of the Punong Barangay considering that under Section 22 (c) of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 , the barangay enters into a contract through its own local chief executive. In entering said contract, it may be

reasonably deduced that the Punong Barangay may no longer act in the public interest due to some private, pecuniary, or other personal considerations that may tend to affect his judgment to the prejudice of the service or the public. Be that as it is, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to the opinion/view of the more authoritative agency. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, RITY OF THE SECR TARY: R VB. DINO Undersecretary for Barangay Affairs LS/17
